coverage_note: Municipal employees under the Municipal Employees' Arbitration Act, R.I. Gen. Laws chapter 28-9.4, administered through the State Labor Relations Act (chapter 28-7). Firefighters (28-9.1), police (28-9.2), certified teachers (28-9.3) and state employees (36-11) have their own chapters and are not covered by this row.

governing_statute.value: Municipal Employees' Arbitration Act, R.I. Gen. Laws chapter 28-9.4, with unfair labor practice procedure under the State Labor Relations Act, chapter 28-7
governing_statute.quote: It is declared to be the public policy of this state to accord to municipal employees the right to organize, to be represented, to negotiate, and to bargain on a collective basis with municipal employers, covering hours, salary, working conditions and other terms of employment

source.publisher: State of Rhode Island General Assembly

labor_board.value: Rhode Island State Labor Relations Board (seven members: three labor, three management, one public), in the Department of Labor and Training
labor_board.quote: There is created in the department of labor and training a board to be known as the Rhode Island state labor relations board that shall be composed of seven (7) members who shall be appointed by the governor, by and with the advice and consent of the senate.

source.publisher: State of Rhode Island General Assembly

supporting.quote: An unfair labor practice charge may be complained of by either the bargaining agent or employer’s representative to the state labor relations board, which shall deal with the complaint in the manner provided in chapter 7 of this title.

ulp_limitation_period.value: Six months from the date of knowledge of the alleged unfair labor practice (Board rule; the statute sets no period)
ulp_limitation_period.quote: Charges must be filed with the Board within six (6) months from the date of knowledge of the alleged unfair labor practice.

source.publisher: Rhode Island Department of State (Code of Regulations)
source.title: 465-RICR-10-00-1 Labor Relations Board - Policy and Procedures

who_may_bargain.value: Municipal employees of cities, towns, districts, school boards and housing and other authorities, excluding elected and administrative officials, board members, certified teachers, police and firefighters (separate chapters), confidential and supervisory, casual and seasonal employees, and some part-time authority employees
who_may_bargain.quote: (b) “Municipal employee” means any employee of a municipal employer, whether or not in the classified service of the municipal employer, except: (1) Elected officials and administrative officials; (2) Board and commission members; (3) Certified teachers, police officers, and firefighters; (4) Confidential and supervisory employees;

source.publisher: State of Rhode Island General Assembly
source.title: R.I. Gen. Laws 28-9.4-2

scope_of_bargaining.value: Hours, salary, working conditions and all other terms and conditions of employment; school-district health benefit plans must be authorized under chapter 27-73; contracts limited to three years (five under a budget commission, receiver or critical-status pension plan)
scope_of_bargaining.quote: shall have the right to negotiate and to bargain collectively with their respective municipal employers and to be represented by an employee organization in the negotiation or collective bargaining concerning hours, salary, working conditions, and all other terms and conditions of employment.

impasse_procedure.value: After 30 days without agreement, mediation through the Director of Labor and Training (compulsory mediation near the appropriation date and contract expiration), then arbitration on request; the award binds on matters not involving the expenditure of money and is advisory on money matters
impasse_procedure.quote: If mediation and conciliation fail or are not requested at any time after the thirty (30) days, either party may request that any and all unresolved issues shall be submitted to arbitration by sending the request by certified mail postage prepaid to the other party, setting forth the issues to be arbitrated.

source.publisher: State of Rhode Island General Assembly
source.title: R.I. Gen. Laws 28-9.4-10

supporting.quote: The decision of the arbitrators shall be made public and shall be binding upon the municipal employees in the appropriate bargaining unit and their representative and the municipal employer on all matters not involving the expenditure of money.

strike_legality.value: Prohibited: strikes, work stoppages and slowdowns by covered municipal employees are illegal
strike_legality.quote: Municipal employees covered by the provisions of this chapter shall not have the right to engage in any strike, work stoppage, or slowdown strike; and any strike, work stoppage, or slowdown strike shall be illegal.

agency_fee_status.value: Not enforceable against nonconsenting public employees after Janus v. AFSCME Council 31 (2018); no Rhode Island fee provision was captured for this row
agency_fee_status.quote: For these reasons, States and public-sector unions may no longer extract agency fees from nonconsenting employees.

dfr_forum.null_reason: Chapter 28-9.4 and the public-sector union unfair labor practices in 28-7-13.1 do not name a duty of fair representation; the forum for such claims rests on case law that was not captured. The Board rules (465-RICR-10-00-1, section 1.22(A)) let an employee file a charge directly when the exclusive agent refuses to file one.
